// diagnostic E0999

Jet.StackedRuleLines

Teaching: stacked `#[…]` rule lines → one `#[A, B]` list or lone `#A`

What

Teaching: stacked `#[…]` rule lines → one `#[A, B]` list or lone `#A`

Why

Rules on one declaration are written once, as one list or one lone rule, so a reader sees them together

Fix

Combine stacked rules into one `#[A, B]` list or a lone `#A`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.StackedRuleLines: Tests/UI/Effects/type_cap_repeated_is_e0999.stderr.

Error: Jet.StackedRuleLines: `#FX` is already applied to this type
  --> Tests/UI/Effects/type_cap_repeated_is_e0999.jet:1:11
    |
  1 | #[FX(IO), FX(!IO)]
    |           ^^^^^^^
 Why: A cap is one list, so a second `#FX` marker can only repeat or disagree with the first
 Fix: Merge both lists into one `#FX(…)` marker
More: jet-lang.dev/e/Jet.StackedRuleLines
